name: imperfect subjunctive
title: Spanish Imperfect Subjunctive Practice: Si Clauses and Quiz
description: Practice the Spanish imperfect subjunctive: forms from the preterite, hablara, tuviera, si clauses and ojalá, with a rule table and 10 sentences checked as you tap.
answer: To form the imperfect subjunctive, take the ellos form of the preterite, drop -ron and add -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -ran: hablaron → hablara, tuvieron → tuviera, fueron → fuera. Nosotros takes an accent: habláramos. Use it after a past trigger (quería que vinieras), in si clauses with the conditional and after ojalá for unlikely wishes.

demand.source: Google autocomplete for US searchers (hl=en, gl=us), docs/seo-plan/us1000/suggest-us-20261127b.csv

rules.example: tuvieron → tuviera, hicieron → hiciera, dijeron → dijera

rules.meaning: wish, emotion, doubt in the past

rules.example: Habla como si fuera el jefe.

quiz.why: After si in a hypothetical: imperfect subjunctive.
Past wish + que: subjunctive, leyéramos with accent.

quiz.after: sol mañana, pero dicen que va a llover.

quiz.why: Pedir que in the past: dijera, from dijeron.
Como si always takes the imperfect subjunctive.
Si yo fuera tú: the classic hypothetical.
Impersonal expression in the past: llegaran.

quiz.before: Mis padres se alegraron de que yo

quiz.why: Nosotros form needs the accent: trabajáramos.

mistakes: Using the conditional after si: «si tendría tiempo» should be «si tuviera tiempo».
Building from the infinitive: «tenera» should be «tuviera»; always start from the ellos preterite.
Forgetting the nosotros accent: «fueramos» should be «fuéramos».
Using the present subjunctive after a past trigger: «quería que vengas» should be «quería que vinieras».
Mixing the -se and -ra endings in one sentence: both are correct (hablara, hablase), but -ra is far more common in the Americas.

heritage: Heritage speakers often use the imperfect subjunctive naturally («si fuera rico»), but in some regions you will also hear the conditional in both halves («si tendría, compraría»). For writing and the AP exam, use si + imperfect subjunctive. Also check the accent in the nosotros form.
teacher: Run «¿Qué harías si…?» chains: one student finishes a sentence with a conditional and the next one turns it into a new si clause. Si ganara la lotería, viajaría; si viajara, iría a Japón…

faq.question: How do you form the imperfect subjunctive?
faq.answer: Start from the ellos form of the preterite, remove -ron and add -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -ran. Every irregularity of the preterite carries over: pidieron → pidiera, durmieron → durmiera, fueron → fuera.

faq.question: What is the difference between -ra and -se?
faq.answer: Hablara and hablase mean the same and both are correct. The -ra form is much more common in Latin America and in US Spanish; -se is more frequent in Spain and in literature.

faq.question: When do I use the imperfect subjunctive instead of the present subjunctive?
faq.answer: When the trigger is in the past or the conditional (quería que, me pidió que, sería bueno que) and in hypothetical si clauses. With a present trigger, use the present subjunctive: quiero que vengas.
